**Test image**: Dried tan/straw-colored corn stalk with diamond-shaped darker lesions on the internode, brown node coloration, and dried stalk background — clearly a stalk disease.

**Reference comparison summary**:
- **Diplodia_Stalk_Rot** (Corn_Disease_28): Most similar — same tan/straw stalk color, small dark pycnidia markings on internode surface, identical background of dried stalks, dark nodes
- **Charcoal_Stalk_Rot**: Shows split internal black tissue — different
- **Physoderma_Stalk_Rot**: Black spots on green stalk — different
- **Anthracnose**: Dark/black shiny lesions with pink coloring — different
- **Bacterial_Stalk_Rot**: Wet/slimy decay — different
- **Fusarium/Gibberella**: Ear rot diseases — different plant part
- **Tar_Spot, Gray_Leaf_Spot, NLB, Eyespot**: Leaf diseases — different plant part

The tan dried stalk with dark markings at internodes and brown nodes most closely matches Diplodia Stalk Rot reference images.
